description: Single call to claude-sonnet-5-5 at high effort with one well-written stylist prompt.
label: smoke

results.requestText: Surprise me — put together something I wouldn't normally think of.

looks.title: The Blazer You Never Wore
looks.idea: Rust check tailoring over tonal navy and cobalt: a sharp pitch look you wouldn't have put together.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the fine cobalt merino into the cigarette trousers so the waist shows under the oversized blazer. Roll the blazer sleeves once to show the cuff. Knot the rust, navy and cream silk scarf loosely at the neck, with the rust picking up the check. Wear the trousers cropped over the Chelsea boots to show a little ankle. Put the camel coat over the top for the Tube.
looks.why: The blazer has never been worn, and it is the polish you want for pitches without defaulting to black. The slim navy trouser balances the oversized jacket, so you avoid the swamped top-and-bottom volume that didn't work before. Cobalt next to rust and camel is a warm, flattering mix. The scarf and hoops add the personality, and arms stay covered. The flat Chelsea boots handle the drizzle.

looks.title: Velvet, Underneath a Shirt
looks.idea: A romantic slip dress worn like a pinafore over a crisp ivory shirt: evening fabric in daylight.
looks.howToWear: Layer the emerald velvet slip over the ivory silk shirt with the collar out and the sleeves rolled to the elbow. Cinch the wide black belt over the dress at the waist. Add black opaque tights and the flat knee-high boots so the midi hem and boot top almost meet. Pop the burgundy beret on at an angle and carry the red mini bag. Wear the trench belted over the top.
looks.why: The belt marks your waist on a bias-cut dress, and emerald is one of your best colours. Ivory next to your face is softer than black. The shirt gives sleeves and a dressier, more polished feel without a blazer, so you avoid the corporate-black trap. Burgundy and red are warm and joyful. Tights, boots and the water-resistant trench suit 9°C and drizzle.

looks.title: Pink Tweed, Camel Cord
looks.idea: Hot pink and orange abstract print under a cropped boucle jacket, grounded by 70s corduroy.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the camp-collar shirt fully into the high-rise flares and leave the collar open over the neckline of the cropped tweed jacket. The jacket stops at the waist, so the waist line stays defined. Let the flare hem sit over the Chelsea boots. Wear the orange-pink resin earrings with no other jewellery. Throw the leopard faux-fur coat over the top and carry the red mini bag.
looks.why: This is the most surprising look, and it is one for the weekend market or a gallery visit. It has your print-led, romantic-with-one-sharp-element sensibility: a big abstract print, a tweed jacket, and camel to settle it. The cropped jacket and high-rise flares flatter your waist and torso-to-leg proportions. The tweed covers the short sleeves, and the faux-fur coat keeps you warm and adds joy. It's two under-worn pieces, and the camel keeps the colour warm rather than loud.

output.note: I left out the mint blouse and powder blue skirt as icy pastels that drain you, and the suede boots because of the drizzle. The checked blazer look is the one I'd wear for a client pitch.

failures.detail: Ankle-cropped m27 with flat black m60 and a strip of bare ankle slices her short legs. The hip-length boyfriend m45 then sits over the high waist, so the tucked m10 does little to mark it. A high-rise full-length leg would have lengthened her.
Under the new blazer, navy and cobalt solids are the safe, familiar base. The only print conversation is a small scarf, which is thin for a print-led client who asked to be surprised.
It never explains why black m60 belongs in a rust, camel and navy palette. It also skips the bulk of layering the oversized m45 under the straight-cut m50 coat.

looks.comment: This is the right instinct: finally putting m45 to work for pitches without falling back on the black m40. The execution is careful rather than exciting, though, and the cropped slim trouser undercuts both her leg line and the eclecticism the check could have unlocked.

failures.detail: There is no print anywhere for a client whose DNA is print-led. The m84 scarf or m66 leopard loafers on a drier day would have brought it back to her.

The black m85 belt, m88 tights, m67 boots and m51 trench stack up into a lot of black on a warm palette. A wide black belt cinched over bias-cut velvet and a relaxed silk shirt also risks bunching at the waist.
Beret, slip-over-shirt and knee boots together tip toward a stock Parisian schoolgirl image. Dropping m87, or swapping the belt, would keep it hers.

looks.comment: This is the genuine surprise of the edit. It wakes up the once-worn m38 in a way she wouldn't have tried, with emerald, ivory, burgundy and red all in her warm range. It needs one print and a little less black to feel like Maya rather than a mood board.

failures.detail: The large-scale m12 print is buried under the boxy m42 jacket and then the oversized m52 fur. Only a collar and a sliver of print would show.
The look stacks volume on top: oversized shirt, boxy boucle and an oversized fur coat, all over flares. That is the same swamped top-and-bottom volume as her failed tulle-skirt-and-chunky-knit look.
Faux fur m52 mats in drizzle. Corduroy flares worn over flat boots will drag and wick water at the hem.
Flares need a heel to lengthen short legs. Over flat m60 they pool and shorten her.

The explanation claims camel keeps it 'warm rather than loud' while the outfit piles hot pink, orange, leopard and red together. It also claims the romantic-with-one-sharp-element formula when nothing here is sharp.

looks.comment: Pink on pink with orange is a real Susie Bubble idea and uses two under-worn pieces, but there are too many soft, voluminous layers fighting each other. Swap the fur for m51 or m50 and let the shirt show, or drop m42 entirely.

judgement.missedOpportunity: m45 check blazer + m20 navy floral wide-leg trousers + m10 cobalt merino tucked in + m62 red patent Mary Janes (patent copes with drizzle) + m80 hoops + m74 red mini bag + m51 trench. This is check-on-floral print-mixing built on her proven floral-plus-cobalt look. The high-rise full-length leg lengthens her, the blazer adds pitch polish, and it is a true surprise.
judgement.summary: This is a thoughtful edit that reaches for the right neglected pieces (m45, m38, m42, m12) and respects the directives and the drizzle better than most. None of the three looks quite lands. Look 1 is polished but timid, and its cropped trouser works against her leg line. Look 2 is the most original but drops print entirely and leans on too much black. Look 3 has the most personality but smothers its own print under two bulky layers and puts faux fur in the rain. The obvious winner, m45 over the floral m20 trousers, was sitting right there. Send Looks 1 and 2 with tweaks; rework Look 3.

results.requestText: Wedding guest — outdoor afternoon ceremony, and the forecast says it might rain.

looks.title: Baroque Romantic
looks.idea: Her most proven dress, made wedding-ready with warm gold and a camel topcoat.
looks.howToWear: Wear the wrap dress with sheer-feel black tights. If the tights are opaque, the 60 denier pair is fine. Tie the wrap snugly at the natural waist. Layer the camel coat over it, open, so the burgundy-and-gold print shows down the front. Stack the gold bangles on one wrist and keep the chunky hoops as the only earrings. Carry the tan crossbody on a short strap so it sits at the hip and doesn't interrupt the waist.
looks.why: This is the spirit of the look that got her the most compliments, and it is already long-sleeved, waisted and midi-length for 9°C. The burgundy, gold and navy sit well against her warm colouring. A 5cm block heel is well under her 7cm limit and holds up better on grass than a stiletto. The suede is the only weak spot in drizzle, so if the rain turns heavy, swap in the black flat knee-high boots (m67).

looks.title: Emerald and Pink Tweed
looks.idea: Velvet, tweed and pearls: joyful colour with one sharp, structured jacket.
looks.howToWear: Wear the emerald velvet slip with black opaque tights and the flat knee-high boots. Put the cropped pink tweed jacket over the slip and leave it open so the bias cut skims the hips. The jacket's cropped hem sits at her waist, which keeps her proportions. Add the pearl drops and carry the red mini bag on its short strap. Wear the belted trench over everything for the walk in and the drizzle. Cinch it, and take it off for photos.
looks.why: Emerald is one of her best colours, and the pink and red make it feel romantic and a bit Gucci, but toned down. The tweed jacket gives the slip sleeves and a polished edge, without the corporate black blazer that flattened her red dress before. Flat boots and water-resistant outerwear suit an outdoor, damp ceremony. This also brings in two under-worn pieces, the velvet slip and the tweed jacket.

looks.title: Floral Trousers, Gold and Check
looks.idea: A print-on-print trouser suit-style look with a cinched waist and gold for the occasion.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the gold satin camisole into the high-rise floral trousers. Put the oversized check blazer over it, worn open. Roll or push the sleeves up to the forearm, then cinch the blazer with the wide black belt at the natural waist so the volume stays controlled. Knot the silk floral scarf onto the tan bag's strap, so the rust picks up the blazer check. Wear the red patent Mary Janes and the resin flower earrings. Add the gold bangles on the wrist. Camel coat over the top outside.
looks.why: The belted blazer solves the volume issue by creating an hourglass waist, so she doesn't get swamped like she did in the tulle and jumper look. The floral trousers, gold cami and rust check are warm tones that echo each other, and the red patent flats repeat her colour-on-colour success. The result is a trouser option that is eclectic and print-mixed, and it gives the never-worn check blazer an outfit at last. The flats, with a full-length hem, are practical on wet grass. The gold satin is the dressy touch for a wedding, and the blazer keeps her warm and covered.

output.note: There is no umbrella in the wardrobe, so bring one, as none of these looks include it. Wedding etiquette-wise I left out the ivory shirt, the cream cable knit and the white pieces to avoid the bridal palette. I also skipped the mint blouse and the powder blue tulle skirt, because those icy colours drain her. The strongest wedding-formal pieces she owns (the saffron beaded maxi and the black lace dress) are sleeveless and too cold for a 9°C outdoor ceremony without a lot of layers, so I kept them in reserve for an evening reception if one is on the day.

failures.detail: It leads with the m61 suede boots for an outdoor ceremony on grass, in drizzle, with rain forecast. The stylist's own note says the suede is not for rain. m67 is offered only as a 'heavy rain' swap when it should have been the default.

Black 60-denier tights (m88) break into tan ankle boots (m61) right at the ankle. On a client with short legs relative to her torso, that cuts the leg line. Black knee-highs (m67) over the same tights would give one continuous column.
This is essentially the gallery-opening outfit repeated with her most-worn coat (m50) and bag (m70). Nothing lifts it to wedding level.
'Wear with sheer-feel black tights. If the tights are opaque, the 60 denier pair is fine' is muddled filler. m88 is the only pair she owns, and it is opaque.

looks.comment: Right dress: long-sleeved, waisted, formality 4 and proven on her. But it is styled as a rerun of a gallery night, on the one pair of shoes that fails the weather. Swap to m67 as the lead, and add one wedding-specific lift such as pearls m81 or the pink tweed m42, and this becomes a confident send.

failures.detail: At 9°C outdoors, a velvet slip (m38) under a boxy cropped boucle jacket (m42) is too light to stand through a ceremony. 'Take the trench off for photos' means she will be cold for most of the day.

With the black trench (m51) worn over black tights (m88) and black knee boots (m67), the outdoor version of this look is head-to-toe black. That hides the emerald and pink, and puts stark black at her face. It echoes the 'black layer flattens the colour' lesson from her known miss.
A boxy cropped jacket worn open over a bias-cut slip does not mark her waist as claimed. It squares off the torso. Her hourglass shape and defined waist are lost.
Velvet marks badly with water, which is a real rain risk, and the explanation never raises it. It also claims waist definition the silhouette does not deliver.

looks.comment: This is the look with the real idea: emerald velvet, pink tweed, pearls and a red bag is a genuinely Michele-lite, joyful wedding outfit, and it uses two under-worn pieces. The outerwear choice and the cold undermine it. Swap the black trench for the camel coat m50 with an umbrella, or at least explain how to keep the colour visible.

failures.detail: Full-length wide-leg crepe trousers (m20) with flat Mary Janes (m62) will drag and wick water on wet grass. The stylist claims the opposite. The feet are also bare in thin flats at 9°C. Sleeves pushed up under a longline coat is cold, and fussy.

The navy/pink/green floral (m20) and the brown/rust/cream large check (m45) share no colour. The only bridge is a scarf (m84) knotted on a bag strap at the hip, away from the body. Calling the trousers 'warm tones that echo each other' is wrong, because navy is their base.

An oversized wool boyfriend blazer cinched with a black belt bunches. A longline camel coat (m50) over that adds a third bulky layer. The black belt (m85) also drops an unrelated hard black into a brown/navy/gold palette.
Resin flower earrings (m83, formality 2/5) plus a camp-level pile-up of floral, check, gold satin, red patent and a scarf reads as a gallery or market look, not an afternoon wedding.
The rationale rests on false claims: that flats with a full-length hem are 'practical on wet grass', and that the tones are 'warm'.

looks.comment: It is good to try to give the never-worn m45 a home, and a trouser option is useful. But this is too many competing elements with no shared colour logic, and it fails the wet-grass test. Save it for an indoor creative event, edited down to three statements.

judgement.missedOpportunity: Elevate her proven dress for the wedding and the weather. Baroque wrap m30 with black opaque tights m88 and black flat knee-high boots m67: rain-safe, and one unbroken dark leg line. Add the pink tweed cropped jacket m42 over the wrap: pink against burgundy reads romantic, the cropped hem sits at the tied waist, and it gives the sharp element plus warmth. Pearl drops m81 make it wedding-specific. The red mini bag m74 adds a colour pop. The camel coat m50 goes over it for warmth, with an umbrella.
judgement.summary: Sensible editing in the note: bridal whites and icy pastels avoided, the umbrella gap flagged, and an honest reason for parking the sleeveless formal dresses. But the weather is treated as an afterthought. Look 1 leads with suede, Look 2 depends on taking the coat off at 9°C and smothers its colour in black, and Look 3 sends full-length crepe and bare flats onto wet grass with an unbridged print clash. Look 2 has the genuine creative idea and Look 1 has the right dress. Neither is finished to a standard I would send to a paying client without revisions to shoes, outerwear and waist definition.

results.requestText: Surprise me — put together something I wouldn't normally think of.

looks.title: Slip Over Cargo
looks.idea: Satin slip dress layered over cargos and a faded band tee, so a dressy piece gets the club-kid treatment.
looks.howToWear: Wear the band tee under the slip dress so the sleeves and boxy hem show below the satin. Pull the dress down over the cargo trousers so the midi hem sits at mid-calf. Leave the cargo hems loose over the boots, or push them into the boots if they catch the chain. Wear the chunky chain over the dress straps. Keep the cropped puffer unzipped to show the satin layers.
looks.why: You'd normally keep the slip dress for going out, but over trousers it's warm and wind-proof, and there's no skirt to blow around on the bike. The satin against faded cotton and nylon is the same undone, music-led mix as Berlin club style. The long dress balances the boxy tee and the short puffer, which suits your oversized-with-contrast taste.

looks.title: Tartan Over Jeans
looks.idea: A red tartan mini worn over baggy jeans in the 90s grunge way, with a hoodie as the soft base.
looks.howToWear: Pull on the baggy jeans first and wear them low. Tuck the front of the hoodie into the skirt waistband and leave the back loose, so the skirt sits as a short layer over the jeans. Put the hood out over the collar of the leather jacket. Stack the jean hems over the lace-up boots and leave them a bit scrunched. Wear the jacket open.
looks.why: Your favourite gig outfit is hoodie, tartan and boots, so this keeps the same ingredients but changes the shape. The jeans make it much warmer for 4°C wind than bare tights would, and the tartan is the red that suits your high-contrast colouring. The short skirt over the baggy jeans gives you the fitted-or-short balance you like against the oversized hoodie. The brown leather jacket adds the vintage touch, and you can cycle in all of it.

looks.title: Green on Green
looks.idea: A chunky forest green jumper over a faded band tee, with the green trainers picking up the colour, in a relaxed, undone outfit.
looks.howToWear: Wear the band tee under the jumper and pull its hem out about 5cm below the knit for a layered edge. Push the jumper sleeves up to the forearm. Wear the jeans low and slightly cuffed so the green and white trainers show. Put the chain over the neckline of the jumper. Zip the cropped puffer to the chest and leave the rest of it open over the long jumper.
looks.why: The forest green jumper has only been worn 12 times and works well on you, because deep green is one of your colours. Layering a faded band tee under it gives the look a vintage, music-led feel, so it doesn't look neat or preppy. Wearing the jumper long under a cropped puffer keeps your lower back covered in the wind, and the low-top trainers are fine for walking and cycling when it's dry.

output.note: Your wardrobe has no scarf, hat or socks, and those are what you'd want at 4°C with a cold wind, especially in the trainer look. The trainers are fine for a dry day, but switch to the boots if it turns wet or windier.

failures.detail: The cropped puffer l10 is worn open 'to show the satin layers', leaving only a cotton tee and thin satin l08 over the chest at 4°C in a cold wind. It needs to be zipped on the bike.

Calling a satin slip over cargos 'warm and wind-proof' overclaims. The warmth comes from the cargos l06 and the puffer, not the dress. The cycling note worries about the cargo hems catching but never mentions the midi satin hem, which is the bigger snag risk.

looks.comment: This is the genuine surprise the brief asked for. It brings out the barely-worn slip dress l08 in a tonal black, club-kid layering that is pure Berlin and very her. Fix the open puffer and tell her to knot or hitch the satin hem on the bike, and it's ready to send.

failures.detail: The oversized hoodie l01 is half-tucked into an A-line mini l07, which sits over baggy low-slung jeans l05, all under a boxy jacket l09. That piles fleece, wool and denim at the hips and puts volume everywhere. It contradicts her 'oversized plus fitted or short' rule, which the explanation claims it satisfies.
A fleece hoodie under an open, warmth-3 leather jacket is thin for a 4°C wind on a bike.
This is close to a straight remix of her known favourite gig outfit, so it does little to surprise her.

looks.comment: Skirt-over-trousers is a legitimate 90s move, but over baggy, low-slung jeans with a tucked fleece hoodie it turns into a bulky stack. The palette of light-wash blue, grey marl, red tartan and brown is also busier than it needs to be. Swapping l05 for the slimmer-reading black cargos l06 and zipping or closing the jacket would rescue it.

failures.detail: Jumper, tee, jeans, trainers and puffer is an everyday outfit, not something she 'wouldn't normally think of'. It fails the core request.
Low-top trainers l12 with jeans cuffed to show the ankle in a cold 4°C wind.
The chain l14 goes over the jumper neckline, but the puffer is zipped to the chest and hides it. 'Zip to chest, leave the rest open' over a long jumper is an awkward instruction.

looks.comment: Using deep green l04 at the face is a good call for her colouring. Otherwise this is a pleasant, forgettable outfit with a matchy trainer pick-up, and it is not a surprise. It also wastes the green jumper, which could have been the knit-over-satin moment.

judgement.missedOpportunity: The 90s grunge knit-over-satin look: forest green chunky jumper l04 pulled over the black slip dress l08 so the bias-cut satin falls out beneath the cable knit. Add black opaque tights l13, lace-up boots l11, the chain l14 over the knit, and the cropped puffer l10 zipped. It is surprising, it puts deep green at the face, it pairs oversized on top with a fluid column below, and it is warm enough. For the bike, she can add the cargos l06 under the dress or knot the hem.
judgement.summary: Look 1 is a real find. It answers 'surprise me' with an under-used piece and a club-style idea that is clearly hers, needing only a zipped puffer and a note about the satin hem. Look 2 is a near-copy of her favourite outfit with a bulky skirt-over-baggy-jeans proportion and too little warmth. Look 3 is a safe default that ignores the brief. The note about missing scarf and hat is honest and useful, but the set leans on one strong idea and two weak ones. The green jumper and slip dress were never put together, though that pairing is the obvious showstopper.

results.requestText: Wedding guest — outdoor afternoon ceremony, and the forecast says it might rain.

looks.title: Black Slip, Puffer Edge
looks.idea: Satin slip as the wedding-appropriate piece, roughed up with a puffer and boots so it stays undone and not polished.
looks.howToWear: Wear the slip dress over the opaque tights and lace the boots up fully, with the dress hem falling just above the boot top. Zip the cropped puffer to mid-chest so the thin straps and satin neckline show. Let the chain sit over the neckline, outside the puffer if you open it for the ceremony. Put your essentials in the tote and cross it over your body to cycle.
looks.why: It's the dressiest thing she owns, and the black, bias-cut midi gives wedding-level respect without anything preppy or corporate. Her guaranteed gig combo of boots and tights keeps it hers. The nylon puffer is also the most rain-tolerant layer she has, and the tights and cropped puffer handle 4°C and wind. The midi on tights is fine for walking and cycling.

looks.title: Tartan and Forest Green
looks.idea: Her gig-night tartan skirt with a deep green jumper: rich autumn colour, oversized on top and short below.
looks.howToWear: Half-tuck the front of the chunky jumper into the tartan mini, or leave it loose if you prefer the bigger shape. Wear the opaque tights and the boots. Layer the cropped puffer on top so the jumper hem hangs below it. Wear the chain over the knit.
looks.why: It repeats the spirit of her favourite gig outfit, swapping the grey hoodie for the green jumper, which is the most dressed-up top she has. Red, black and deep green all suit her high-contrast colouring, and the wool skirt, jumper, tights and puffer are the warmest combination for standing outside. The mini and tights are easy to cycle in.

looks.title: Cargo Black, White Tank
looks.idea: All-black base with a white tank and leather jacket: a Berlin club-wedding guest.
looks.howToWear: Wear the opaque tights under the cargos as a thermal base layer. Tuck the white tank in fully and add the chain on top. Wear the leather jacket open over it and roll the cargo hems once so the chunky boots show. Keep the boots laced.
looks.why: This is the most her option: relaxed, a bit undone, and sharper with the white tank and vintage leather. The tights under the cargos block the wind for the bike ride. Of the three it is the lightest on top, so it suits a short ceremony and the cycle across town. It is the least wedding-formal, but the clean black and white line keeps it intentional.

output.note: Honest gap: her wardrobe has nothing truly formal, no waterproof coat or umbrella, and no dressy shoes. The slip dress look is the closest to wedding dress code. If the rain turns heavy, the nylon puffer and boots are her best protection and leather and satin will not like a downpour.

failures.detail: Unzipping the cropped puffer l10 to mid-chest to show the thin satin straps of l08 leaves the chest and neck open at 4°C in a cold wind. The crop also leaves the torso below it covered only by satin (warmth 1/5). There is no warm layer between the slip and the coat.

l15 is a large canvas tote, not a crossbody. 'Cross it over your body to cycle' won't work in practice, and a big shopping tote is the weakest note at a wedding. A bias-cut satin midi on a bike also needs a practical tip, such as knotting or clipping the hem away from the chain. None is given.
It misses the obvious 90s-grunge move of layering the oversized forest-green jumper l04 over the slip so the satin skirt shows below. That would solve the warmth problem and add colour.

looks.comment: Right anchor and right instinct: l08 roughed up with l13, l11 and l10 is the closest this wardrobe gets to wedding-appropriate, and it still feels Berlin. But as written she will be freezing at the neckline and midriff during an outdoor ceremony, and the tote advice doesn't work.

failures.detail: This is essentially her gig outfit (l07 + l13 + l11) with the top swapped. Respectful enough, but nothing in it marks the day as a wedding rather than a bar night.
Chunky oversized l04 hanging below cropped puffer l10, over an A-line mini, risks swallowing the skirt into one big blob on top. The half-tuck should be the instruction, not optional.
No bag specified, and nothing to address rain beyond the puffer.

looks.comment: Warm, practical and true to her, and red, black and forest green suit her high contrast. But red tartan with green cable knit drifts towards Christmas and nearly preppy. The chain l14 and boots l11 are doing a lot to keep it grunge.

failures.detail: A rib tank l03 (warmth 1/5) under an open leather jacket l09 at 4°C with cold wind is a non-starter for an outdoor ceremony. Leather is also the worst layer she owns for possible rain.
Cargo trousers l06 and a vest tank are the least formal pieces she owns. Calling it a 'club-wedding guest' doesn't make it wedding-appropriate.
'Lightest on top, so it suits a short ceremony and the cycle' argues against the brief: 4°C, wind and rain call for more on top, not less.
This is her everyday uniform presented as a third option. It adds range on paper, not real value.

looks.comment: This should not go to the client. It ignores the weather and the occasion, and the tights-under-cargos trick doesn't rescue a bare-armed top half in a cold wind.

judgement.missedOpportunity: Black satin slip l08 with the forest-green chunky jumper l04 worn over it, satin midi showing below. Add black opaque tights l13, lace-up boots l11, cropped puffer l10 fully zipped for the ceremony walk, and the chain l14 over the knit. It's the classic 90s-grunge slip-and-sweater: wedding-respectful from the dress, warm and wind-proof from the knit, rain-tolerant from the puffer and boots, and a deep green/black palette that flatters her high contrast. Swap the tote for whatever small bag she can borrow, or carry essentials in the puffer pockets.
judgement.summary: The honest note about the wardrobe's gaps is good, and Look 1 has the right anchor. But the stylist kept treating 4°C wind and rain as an afterthought. Look 1 exposes the chest and midriff, and Look 3 puts her in a tank top under leather. Look 2 is warm and very her, but it reads more gig than wedding. The strongest answer was to merge Looks 1 and 2: slip dress l08 under jumper l04, then tights, boots and puffer. Send Look 1 reworked with that layer and Look 2 with a firm half-tuck. Drop Look 3.
